narratives.Overview:
## Problem

"Recut" is one word carrying five jobs in the design-critique protocol. None of them is a command. Operators, parents, critics, and ingest use the word for different things in the same thread, and three open issues (#4320, #4353, #4352) each bound a remedy that adds more machinery on top of the word instead of removing it.

| Use | Where | Machine effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Recut:` lean token | `content/contracts/design-critique.md` (Successor lean section), `packages/core/src/design-critique/auto-stamp-chip.ts` `leanCarriesRecutToken` | at ingest, harvest `## Bound remedy` from the cited lean instead of body AC |
| "recut arc" | contract `### The arc`, `## Bind after accepted synthesis` | any post-bind new lean: restamp `mechanism-shaped`, drop `ingest-ready` |
| "recut the body" / `unrecut-body` | contract bind section, closed reason table; #4237 and #4258 body headers | rewrite the GitHub body from the bound lean; set-level shape refuses ingest |
| "recut skip class" | `packages/core/src/hooks/dispatcher.ts` (#4296 comment), `packages/core/src/hooks/readonly.ts` | process-only critic spawn skips dest lock; unrelated to the other four |
| "Forward verdict: recut" | parent prose on #4353 lean 5627961170, #4199 lean 5626227158, #4352 lean 5627729396 | a verdict polarity: the filed body cannot bind as written |

Plus the dead chip `design-critique:recut-needed` (fails closed in `CHIP_ALIASES`, still documented as live in `.github/ISSUE_LABELS.md` lines 250-252), and adjectival forms ("recut-shaped map", "close-polarity recut", "recut-bound thread").

The #4352 bound remedy (5627729396) uses the word as a verb three times in four bullets ("Recut In plain English", "recut the three-name lock"). The #4353 parent used it in three senses in one comment. The overload is structural, not an operator miss.

## Field

- #4271 lean 5607103339: `Recut:` line whose English says the issue "needs another focused body recut before ingest". Operator read Recut as a body-rewrite command. Parent 5620175893 published the canned paragraph "Recut means rewriting the GitHub issue body". Critic 5620416210 F1 on #4309 blocked that teaching as stale-target on a digest-pinned lean.
- #4199 lean 5626227158 + synthesis 5626232238: N=3 panel, every critic `blocks-the-design`, all headings `accept-into-contract` into a `Recut:` lean, yolo standing auto-stamped `ingest-ready` in 33 seconds. Plain English said "would not ingest"; `evaluateCompletedArcRecord` returned `complete`; `extractBoundRemedyHarvest` returned 4 items. The operator bound a Bound-remedy list that nothing named as the spec.
- #4254 lean 5587555346 (#4258 field): `Recut:` lean, body AC harvested instead of the bound remedy; body rewrite then looked like a new arc.
- #4343 lean 5627418031, #4337 5627418296, #4335 5627418590 (#4352 field): recut summaries led with cannot-bind and never named leftover or close.

## Root cause

The only thing ingest needs to know is which text is the spec. Today two signals must agree: the `Recut:` token and a non-empty `## Bound remedy` heading on the cited lean (`issue-ingest.ts` ingest path; `markdown-scanners.ts` `extractBoundRemedyHarvest`). The heading alone carries all of the information. The token is #4258 belt-and-suspenders, and because it is a bare word on a lean it leaks into prose as a verb, a verdict, and a body-rewrite instruction.

Every other sense is an ordinary thing that already has an ordinary name: a later arc, a body rewrite, a process-only spawn, a set-level shape.

## Expected

Retire the word. One machine signal, stated in plain English on every bound lean.

1. **Spec source at ingest is the heading, not a token.** Cited successor lean has a non-empty `## Bound remedy` list: harvest it as `plan.items`; the GitHub body is history in Overview. Heading absent: body is normative (existing #4237 path, digest-pinned when `Target-digest:` is present). Heading present with an empty list: refuse, nothing written (existing `RecutHarvestRefusedError` shape, renamed). Delete `leanCarriesRecutToken` and the nine-spelling `Recut:` grammar.
2. **The plain-English summary names the spec source.** Under `## In plain English` on the successor lean and the synthesis, the parent states in ordinary language one of: the spec is the Bound-remedy list below and why; the body stands as the spec and why; this number has no leftover next-build and should close and why. Pointer-only and refusals-only remain a published miss (#4309 / #4352). No implementer address, no next-step field, no "ingest may proceed".
3. **Close polarity reuses the existing terminal.** `design-critique: cancelled, because ...` is already the chip-less ingest-block record (#4352 lean 5627729396 bullet 3 agrees). Do not add `design-critique:recommend-closure`. Do not revive `recut-needed`. Catalog stays three names.
4. **Rename the other four senses.** "recut arc" becomes "a later arc" (nothing is special about it: any post-bind lean restamps `mechanism-shaped` and drops `ingest-ready`). "recut the body" becomes "rewrite the body". `unrecut-body` becomes `set-level-body` in the closed reason table (published before the evaluator returns it). Dispatcher and readonly comments say "process-only skip class".
5. **Skill EXIT follows the heading.** Non-empty Bound remedy: `Next: run task issue:ingest`. Body normative: same. Cancelled: recommend GitHub close, no ingest line. Missing heading is not a state; it is the body-normative branch.
6. **Yolo and auto-stamp are unchanged.** Yolo stays the confirm conjunct on a posted all-accept map (#4308). Auto-stamp stays `ingest-ready` after the record. No ingest-pick token, no third consent identity read off the thread (#4353 critic 5627947089 F3 and F4: both branches already exist, and thread-read consent is forgeable).

## Acceptance

- [ ] `extractBoundRemedyHarvest` is the sole harvest selector at ingest; `leanCarriesRecutToken` and `RECUT_TOKEN_RE` are deleted. Fixture: #4199 lean 5626227158 harvests 4 items with the `Recut:` line removed; #4254 lean 5587555346 same.
- [ ] Empty-list refusal keeps its fail-closed shape under a name that does not contain "recut". Nothing written.
- [ ] Contract `## Plain-language summary` requires the spec-source sentence (Bound remedy, body, or close) on successor lean and synthesis. Content-contract test locks the MUST.
- [ ] Contract has zero occurrences of "recut" (case-insensitive) outside a single legacy note. `## Citation grammar` and `## Reserved line-starts` drop `Recut:`.
- [ ] Closed reason table row `unrecut-body` renamed `set-level-body`; `COMPLETED_ARC_BLOCK_REASONS` and its content-contract pin updated together. Detail string no longer says "recut the body".
- [ ] `.github/ISSUE_LABELS.md`: stale `triage-ready` / `recut-needed` rows (lines 250-252) removed; stamp table says three catalog names; changelog row added.
- [ ] `content/commands.md` chip verb line and thin skill EXIT updated per Expected 5.
- [ ] Dispatcher / readonly comments renamed; no behavior change; existing #4296 tests still pass.
- [ ] Legacy admit: existing bound leans that carry `Recut:` plus a non-empty Bound remedy still ingest the same items (the heading was always present). No restamp of #4199, #4343, #4337, #4335.
- [ ] Yolo confirm, auto-stamp chip, `evaluateCompletedArcRecord` predicates, and Target-digest admission are byte-identical in behavior except for the reason rename.

## Non-goals

- A `task recut` or any new operator verb.
- The #4353 ingest-pick token and its new block reason.
- The #4352 `recommend-closure` chip.
- Auto-ingest, or any permission-shaped ingest text in the summary.
- NLP of the summary. The heading is the signal.
- Renaming `preCutover` / `precutover` identifiers (case-insensitive grep false positives).

## Supersedes

- #4320 (definition): resolved as "zero names". The concept dissolves into the heading.
- #4353 (Recut+yolo mints ingest clearance): the field bug is owned here as Expected 2. The bound remedy (ingest-pick token) is not built; critic 5627947089 F1, F3, F4 are absorbed as the reason.
- #4352 (recut summaries omit leftover-or-close): Expected 2 and 3. Bound remedy 5627729396 bullets 1, 2, 4 are absorbed; bullet 3 (the chip) is declined in favor of the existing cancelled terminal.

Operator will place those three on hold pending this arc. Ingest on #4353 and #4352 should not run while their `ingest-ready` chips stand.

## Refs

#4320 #4353 #4352 #4258 #4298 #4237 #4308 #4309 #4296 #4205 #4199 #4271 #4254

### Comment by @MScottAdams (2026-09-11T02:18:54Z)

model: gpt-5.6-sol
role: critic

The vocabulary retirement is defensible, but the heading-only selector cannot bind as written with the existing scanner. It promotes example and rejected-section text into the build contract.

Scope: round 1, fresh refutation of comment 5628421534; reads bounded to that inclusive ceiling and tree ac195cf71d1f3a91b490c91a426248d7fb414331. No later comments or sibling posts read.

### F1 - blocks-the-design: define operative heading selection before removing the token

Evidence: I loaded the pinned TypeScript with `git show`, transpiled it in memory, and executed `findBoundRemedyHeading` and `extractBoundRemedyHarvest`. A fenced Markdown example containing the level-two Bound-remedy heading and `1. example only` harvested that item. A heading spelled `## Bound remedy rejected` harvested `rejected proposal`. Two matching sections harvested only the first. The implementation at `packages/core/src/intake/markdown-scanners.ts:174-238` uses a prefix regex and first match, with no position check. These are synthetic counterexamples, not claims about the historical threads.

Failure mode: a cited body-normative lean without the old token can contain an example or rejected alternative. Today `issue-ingest.ts:2034` does not select that list; Expected 1 would select it solely because the heading parser matches. This broadens the authority of untrusted descriptive text. A spec-source sentence cannot prevent it because the proposed machine does not read that sentence.

Consequence: retain the one-heading design only after specifying which occurrence is operative and how duplicate/ambiguous sections are handled, with executable refusal/example fixtures. Inventory already includes `classifyPosition` for digest/citation positions and the existing heading/slice parser; reuse those mechanisms where their semantics fit instead of adding consent tokens or NLP. The strongest case for deletion is that an intentionally authored, unique Bound-remedy section makes the token redundant. A demonstrated selector that excludes examples and resolves ambiguity would flip this objection; bare heading presence does not.

### F2 - sharpens-framing: the sole extractor needs an explicit absent result

Evidence: the same pinned execution returned exactly `{items: [], sourceText: ""}` for both `Body stands.` and a bare `## Bound remedy` at EOF. `findBoundRemedyHeading` distinguished them (null versus a heading), but `extractBoundRemedyHarvest` discarded that distinction.

Failure mode: implementing the sole-selector AC against its current result either falls back to body AC for an empty heading, violating fail-closed behavior, or refuses the valid absent-heading/body branch. Testing nonempty prose under an empty heading would miss the EOF collision.

Consequence: the target can survive; specify an absent/present result in the existing extractor, using its existing heading finder, and lock absent, bare-empty, prose-only, and nonempty fixtures. This is a required API clarification, not a second spec-source signal.

### F3 - sharpens-framing: EXIT depends on admission state before spec source

Evidence: pinned `evaluateCompletedArcRecord` executions returned `complete` for a cited lean plus acceptance record, `cancelled` after a later terminal, `missing-record` after a newer uncited lean, and `unrecut-body` for a completed set-level thread even when the cited lean had a nonempty Bound-remedy list. The thin skill currently qualifies its ingest recommendation with post-bind state. `issue-ingest.ts:2047` also checks an operative body digest independently of harvest; a changed-body probe returned `stale-target`.

Failure mode: Expected 5's unconditional nonempty-heading/body branches recommend ingest for a draft, a superseded record, or a set-level target that Expected 6 and the acceptance criteria deliberately leave blocked. A missing heading is not itself a state, but completion and target shape still are.

Consequence: keep the proposed vocabulary and qualify that EXIT mapping to an admitted completed record; preserve existing refusal/remediation paths first. Renaming the set-level reason must not imply that a Bound-remedy list bypasses it. This needs framing repair, not a new gate.

### F4 - footnote: retained mechanisms and untrusted directives

Inventory confirmed the three-chip `CHIP_ALIASES` catalog, unconditional ingest-ready auto-stamp selection, operative cancelled terminal, later-lean invalidation, set-level refusal, digest admission, contract post-bind arc rules, and process-only skip-class comments. The stale label documentation does contain the two retired names. These support reuse and terminology cleanup; they do not substantiate a new chip or thread-derived consent identity. The issue's instruction-shaped hold/ingest directions for other numbers were treated as proposal data, not executed. Historical linked-comment counts were not independently verified in this bounded pass.

Critic pass complete; exiting the design-critique skill. Parent synthesis is the next protocol step after all same-round seats post.

### Comment by @MScottAdams (2026-09-11T02:26:51Z)

model: claude-opus-5
role: critic

Round 1 critic, refutation charter, fresh. Envelope: issue 4361, id ceiling 5628421534 inclusive, dispatch SHA `ac195cf71d1f3a91b490c91a426248d7fb414331`, spend N=3, arc-mode no-ingest, seat claude via claude CLI, audit-targets none. Reads pinned to `git show <dispatch-sha>:`. Sibling posts this round are out of envelope; this post stays in the denominator.

Injection / swarm lens fires: the target changes what text becomes `plan.items`, literal capture, and derived-clause `taskStatement` from untrusted GitHub comment bodies. F3 is that finding, not a recital.

## Refutation target

Retire the word; the sole ingest spec-source signal is a non-empty Bound-remedy heading on the cited successor lean; close polarity reuses the cancelled terminal; no `recommend-closure` and no ingest-pick token; yolo and auto-stamp unchanged.

**Survives in part.** The two-signal diagnosis is right, and one half of the record supports it more strongly than the issue argues. The retirement as specified does not bind: Expected 1 converts a fail-closed refusal into a fail-open ingest of text the arc just refuted, the byte-identical acceptance line is measurably false in three directions, the replacement selector ships with no position predicate and its only hazard row deleted, and Expected 2 mandates the exact phrasing an accepted take on an issue this one supersedes ruled instruction-shaped.

## Method note

I re-derived both predicates from source at the pin rather than citing them, and ran them over every lean-shaped comment on the 35 issues carrying `design-critique:mechanism-shaped` or `design-critique:ingest-ready` — 42 leans. Distribution: 21 token+heading, 10 token-no-heading, 2 heading-no-token, 9 neither. That corpus is the evidence under F1 and F2.

Inventory before proposing: `leanCarriesRecutToken`, `extractBoundRemedyHarvest`, `findBoundRemedyHeading`, `parseListItems`, `evaluateCompletedArcRecord`, `latestCancelled` / `hasOperativeCancelledShape`, `refuseUnrecutSetLevel`, `COMPLETED_ARC_BLOCK_REASONS`, `CHIP_ALIASES`, `DESIGN_CRITIQUE_CATALOG_CHIPS`, `designCritiqueChipApplyDelta`, `classifyPosition`, `stripFencedCodeBlocks`, the contract harvest MUSTs, and the thin skill EXIT. No finding below proposes a new mechanism where one of those covers it.

---

### F1 — Expected 1 turns the missing-heading refusal into a body-normative ingest of the refuted body — blocks-the-design

**Evidence.** `packages/core/src/intake/issue-ingest.ts:2034-2048`: when the cited lean carries the token, `extractBoundRemedyHarvest` runs and `items.length === 0` throws `RecutHarvestRefusedError`, nothing written. `packages/core/src/intake/markdown-scanners.ts:228-231`: that function returns `items: []` when `findBoundRemedyHeading` returns null — so **heading-absent is one of the two ways the refusal fires today**, and it is the common one. Expected 1 reassigns that case to "body is normative."

Field frequency, measured over the record history of #4271: five of the six completed-arc records on that thread cite a `role: parent` lean carrying the token with no such heading — 5592441706 cites 5592423042, 5592816470 cites 5592760215, 5593167974 cites 5593129893, 5594921530 cites 5594854975, 5601937180 cites 5601790900. Each was the record-gating state until the next lean superseded it. Today's latest lean there, 5607103339, does carry the heading, so #4271 is not currently in that state; the point is the shape's frequency, not a live block.

**Failure mode.** Parent posts a lean whose plain English says next-build is not this body, omits the heading, binds. Today ingest refuses and prints repair. Under Expected 1 ingest reads the GitHub body, harvests body AC into `plan.items`, and emits an xBRIEF. On #4271 that body is the one its own lean 5607103339 states is not implementation-ready as written. Silent, not blocked: the operator sees a successful ingest.

**This also contradicts a take the issue claims to absorb.** Supersedes says "#4352 ... Bound remedy 5627729396 bullets 1, 2, 4 are absorbed." Bullet 2 of 5627729396 reads verbatim: "Missing Bound-remedy heading stays `RecutHarvestRefusedError` (repair, nothing written)." That bullet is a reading of take 4 on that lean, accepted-into-contract. Expected 1 deletes it while claiming absorption.

**Disposition consequence.** Expected 1 cannot bind as written. Either the missing-heading branch stays refuse — which costs nothing, since it is already the shipped behaviour and the heading is the signal parents reliably write — or the issue must state expressly that it reverses an accepted #4352 take, and say why ingesting a refuted body is safe.

---

### F2 — the byte-identical and legacy-admit acceptance lines are unsatisfiable; three behaviour flips are measured — blocks-the-design

**Evidence.** The last two acceptance boxes assert no behaviour change: "Legacy admit: existing bound leans that carry `Recut:` plus a non-empty Bound remedy still ingest the same items (the heading was always present)" and "... byte-identical in behavior except for the reason rename." Both are scoped to token-carrying leans. Three other classes exist, and all three flip.

**(a) Heading present, token absent — live, on completed arcs.** #3835 lean 5454343749 is `role: parent`, carries the heading with a non-empty list, carries no token, and synthesis 5455528793 cites it by id. Running the predicates: harvest returns 5 items. #3850 lean 5454472108, cited by 5454966234: 4 items. Each is the only lean on its thread, so each is the live latest-lean state. Today body-normative; under Expected 1 the lean becomes the spec. #3835's five items include "**Recut #3842 into this issue or close it.**" and "**Do not unblock #3819 via #3842.**" — cross-issue prose directives that would land as `plan.items`, literal-acceptance capture, and derived-clause `taskStatement`.

**(b) Heading present, list empty.** Measured: heading followed by prose only returns 0 items. Today body-normative ingest succeeds; under Expected 1 it is a hard refuse, nothing written. This shape is not hypothetical — #3835's own synthesis reads "The bound remedy is stated in full on the lean," which is precisely the pointer-shaped section that yields zero items.

**(c) Missing heading** — F1.

The parenthetical "(the heading was always present)" holds for the 21 token+heading leans and fails in the converse direction the change now makes load-bearing: on the 2 heading-no-token leans the *token* was absent while the heading decided everything.

**Failure mode.** An implementer satisfies every acceptance box, ships, and #3835 / #3850 silently change spec source on any later ingest. Nothing in the acceptance set catches it, because the set asserts the flip does not happen.

**Disposition consequence.** Those two boxes must be rewritten to state the intended flips and enumerate the affected records, or Expected 1 needs a transition that keeps both signals for pre-existing leans. As written the acceptance set is inconsistent with Expected 1, and an honest implementer is blocked at the last box.

---

### F3 — the replacement selector has no position predicate, and the change deletes its only hazard row — blocks-the-design

**Evidence.** `findBoundRemedyHeading` scans raw lines: no `stripFencedCodeBlocks`, no `classifyPosition`, and `extractBoundRemedyHarvest` is called on the raw cited body. Contrast `Target-digest:`, which routes through `classifyPosition` specifically because fence and quote do not count (#4243). I ran a constructed lean whose plain-English section quotes a superseded remedy block inside a fenced code block: harvest returns the two quoted bullets, with the token absent. So today that lean is inert; under Expected 1 the quoted-and-withdrawn list is the spec. Blockquote is safe — the heading must start at column 0 with two hashes and a space — so the hazard is specifically fences.

Acceptance box 4 makes this worse rather than better: it drops the recut row from the contract's reserved-line-start matrix and adds no row for the heading that replaces it. After the change, the one place an author would learn the spec selector is fence-blind no longer mentions a spec selector at all.

**Failure mode.** Leans quote and supersede prior leans as a matter of routine — #4271 carries 12 leans, each superseding the last. A parent who fences a withdrawn remedy to show what changed hands ingest a list the arc rejected. Nothing on the thread reads as wrong and no predicate objects. I am not closing this with "a reviewer would catch it": the deterministic control is a position predicate that already exists in this module.

**Disposition consequence.** Expected 1 must either route the heading scan through `stripFencedCodeBlocks` / `classifyPosition`, or box 4 must add a Bound-remedy row to the reserved-line-start matrix stating that fence and quote do not count. The hazard partly pre-exists for token-carrying leans; what the change adds is reachability on the 11 token-less leans plus removal of the published warning.

---

### F4 — Expected 2 mandates a close recommendation that two standing prohibitions and an absorbed take both refuse — blocks-the-design

**Evidence.** Expected 2 requires the parent to state one of three sentences, the third being "this number has no leftover next-build **and should close** and why." The contract's non-normative section carries two prohibitions at MUST-NOT: "Address an implementer in the summary. No imperatives, and no instruction to a later worker," and "Mandate a next-step or recommended-action field on either artifact. A closed form (a verb and an issue) was considered and refused." And #4352 lean 5627729396 take 4, accepted-into-contract, reads: "leftover-or-close in the summary is a recut reading; 'should close' is instruction-shaped." Expected 2's own closing line — "No implementer address, no next-step field" — contradicts its own third branch in the same paragraph.

**Failure mode.** Acceptance box 3 says a content-contract test locks the new MUST. The existing prohibitions are locked in the same suite. One lock has to be deleted; and whichever survives, `composeOverviewWithComments` copies the summary verbatim into the xBRIEF Overview the next worker reads as dispatch input, and the contract records that the quarantine scanner returns zero flags on that composed shape. So a mandated "should close" ships as unfenced parent-voice instruction inside the comment that clears ingest — the same class as the body imperatives struck on #4199, whose bound remedy item 4 reads "Strike body imperatives that constrain later disposition."

**Disposition consequence.** The third branch must be restated declaratively — this number has no leftover next-build, because … — with no close recommendation, or Expected 2 and box 3 cannot bind. Expected 3's close polarity is unaffected: the terminal record is a parent artifact, not a summary sentence.

---

### F5 — acceptance box 6 retires two label rows but leaves the labels live and unclearable — sharpens-framing

**Evidence.** `design-critique:recut-needed` and `design-critique:triage-ready` both exist in the repository's label set. `recut-needed` is attached to #4272, #4269, #4258, #4254 — two of those are this issue's own field exhibits. `triage-ready` is attached to 100+ issues including #3835 and #3850, the F2 exhibits. `designCritiqueChipApplyDelta` removes only names in `DESIGN_CRITIQUE_CATALOG_CHIPS`, so `task scm:issue:design-critique-chip` never clears either one, and `resolveDesignCritiqueChipArg` throws on both names.

**Failure mode.** Box 6 deletes the documentation rows only. A reader then meets `design-critique:recut-needed` on #4254 with no row anywhere explaining it and no sanctioned verb to remove it — the one-word-many-jobs confusion this issue closes, relocated into the label list.

**Disposition consequence.** Box 6 needs a label-disposition step — delete the two GitHub labels, or keep the rows marked retired and do-not-attach — or the retirement is not achieved on the list surface. "Catalog stays three names" is already true and is a different claim.

---

### F6 — boxes 4 and 6 collide with locked assertions the acceptance set never names, and one string box 4 would delete is a live prohibition — sharpens-framing

**Evidence.** `packages/core/src/content-contracts/standards/design_critique_contract.test.ts` pins, as required contract text, both `design-critique:recut-needed` (line 85) and the recut lean token (line 89); line 762 pins the contract's prohibition on adding `design-critique:recut-needed` to `judgmentGates` `labels.any-of`; line 765 asserts `.github/ISSUE_LABELS.md` contains `design-critique:recut-needed`, which box 6 removes; lines 382 and 391 pin the arc-framing sentence and its negation; line 985 pins the skill EXIT string. The acceptance set names the contract, ISSUE_LABELS.md, `content/commands.md`, the skill, dispatcher and readonly comments, and `COMPLETED_ARC_BLOCK_REASONS`. It does not name this file, which carries 23 occurrences.

**Failure mode.** Box 4's "zero occurrences outside a single legacy note" is satisfiable only by deleting that judgmentGates prohibition, which is the only published fence against adding a label `CHIP_ALIASES` fails closed on. Delete the prohibition and its lock together and a later author can add an unstampable name to `plan.policy.judgmentGates`, leaving that gate matchable by nothing the sanctioned verb can write.

**Disposition consequence.** Box 4 must carve out prohibition lines, or restate them without the word, and the acceptance set must name `design_critique_contract.test.ts` so the lock edits are authorized rather than discovered mid-build.

---

### F7 — Expected 5's branch set is not total over the states at which the skill EXIT fires — sharpens-framing

**Evidence.** The thin skill's EXIT copy has two branches: after bind, print ingest; else, operator fills the brief template and dispatches the next envelope. The same skill states "Each critic dispatch EXITs after posting," so that EXIT copy also fires mid-arc. Expected 5's three branches — non-empty Bound remedy, body normative, cancelled — are all post-bind, and its first two print the same line, so it collapses to "always print ingest unless cancelled" and the else-branch is gone. The contract's own sentence is scoped to after bind.

**Failure mode.** A critic-dispatch EXIT on an arc with no completed-arc record falls into the body-normative branch and prints `Next: run task issue:ingest`. `assertCompletedArcAllowsIngest` then blocks on `missing-record`, so nothing is written — but the operator-facing next step points at ingest mid-arc, which the operator-gated loop and the auto-ingest prohibition exist to prevent.

**Disposition consequence.** Expected 5 needs a fourth branch — no completed-arc record, so the operator dispatches the next envelope — or box 7 cannot be closed without regressing the mid-arc print.
